links.outcome: Perceived clinical utility and rate of treatment revision across three weighting/interface schemes
links.effect: Clinician-determined weighting rated higher (4.18) than implicit (3.27, p<0.01) and expert-derived (3.41, p<0.05); prompted treatment revision in 33.3% vs 26.3% implicit and 15.8% expert-derived.
links.quote: Post-hoc analysis indicated that the CDW scheme (Mean: 4.18 ± 0.89) was rated significantly higher than both the Implicit Weighting baseline (Mean: 3.27 ± 0.86 , p < 0.01) and the EDW scheme (Mean: 3.41 ± 1.19 , p < 0.05).

links.outcome: Clinician-adjustable weights versus fixed expert weights: perceived utility and decision change
links.effect: Adjustable clinician-determined weighting rated most useful (4.18 vs 3.41 static) and led to most treatment revisions (33.3% vs 15.8% static); psychiatrists resisted static weights.
links.quote: Of these, the CDW scheme prompted the highest rate of treatment revision: participants changed their initial choice in 33.3% of cases.

unlisted_practices: Letting clinicians set outcome weights (locus of control) in aggregating AI predictions for shared decision-making
